description: Dual-input Mirror SwiGLU: factorized compositional gate/up Views, seed robustness, automatic capacity growth
evidence_level: small CPU synthetic FFN mechanism; NOT a Transformer/language result

teacher.aligned: shared gate/up/down matrices, random distinct gate/up Givens rotations
teacher.partial: aligned teacher plus nine pair-specific residual nonlinear projections
teacher.unrelated: nine independent random gate/up/down SwiGLU matrices

dataset.heldout_condition: aligned only; six seen pairs, three completely untrained pairs
dataset.normalize_metrics: train teacher RMS squared, computed without label noise

dev.selection: common learning rate minimizing arithmetic mean of held-in-pair validation normalized MSE for both teacher families and six methods; no test use

autogrowth.growth_rule: if relative improvement in seen-pair validation normalized MSE is <10% and validation NMSE remains >0.002, add next planes; never use heldout pairs or test

storage.authority: actual torch.save including architecture config, learned float tensors, and small metadata; optimizer excluded
storage.native_lowrank: factor_lora1: more parameters, explicitly separate in analysis

gates.mirror_specific_dual_vs_native: mirror12 >10% lower test NMSE and <=5% worse worst-pair vs gain12, in >=4/5 worlds (paired world seed mean)
gates.factorized_generalization: aligned_holdout mirror12 heldout test NMSE <=0.80x pair_mirror4 and <=0.80x gain12 in >=4/5 worlds
gates.automatic_growth: auto_mirror final test NMSE <=1.10x mirror12 with fewer real inference bytes in >=4/5 aligned_full worlds
gates.compression: aligned_full mirror12 test NMSE <=1.10x independent with <=50% actual bytes in >=4/5 worlds
gates.transfer: no claims about natural language or Transformers; no native superiority if simpler baseline wins

statistics: 5 independent worlds; 2 initializations paired within world. World is independent unit; report ratios of per-world seed means, median and world-cluster uncertainty. Not 10 independent worlds.
runtime: Python 3.13 PyTorch 2.10 CPU float32; OMP/BLAS one thread per process, up to 4 workers, clock not locked; no GPU or quantization
